entry.name: Movement for Reform Judaism (UK)
entry.blurb: The British Reform organization, before its 2026 merger. Not world Reform Judaism.

entry.name: Seesen
entry.desc: Israel Jacobson’s temple inauguration in Seesen (1810) is an early Reform milestone.

entry.name: The Shalom Center
entry.blurb: One of the two organizations named in ALEPH’s account of its 1993 formation. No claim that it then ceased all independent activity.

entry.name: Mecca (Makkah)
entry.desc: Muhammad’s early setting and his point of departure for Medina.

entry.name: Moses
entry.desc: The mediator of the covenant in Exodus 19.

entry.name: Orthodox Judaism
entry.blurb: Orthodox Judaism includes distinct forms of observance and community. Modern Orthodox and Haredi are useful distinctions in the cited US study, not a complete global taxonomy.

notSame.t: Eastern Orthodox Christianity: a shared English word does not identify the same religion.

entry.title: Council of Nicaea
entry.text: Constantine convened the Council of Nicaea. It did not invent Christianity or create the complete biblical canon.

entry.name: Advent (Millerite) movement
entry.blurb: The nineteenth-century Advent movement: antecedent context, not an institutional parent of every Adventist or Witness body.

entry.name: Hafizi Musta’lis
entry.blurb: Hafizi allegiance supported al-Hafiz and later Fatimid imams.

notes.t: A historical node, not a current population estimate.

entry.name: ALEPH: Alliance for Jewish Renewal
entry.blurb: ALEPH describes its formation through the merger of P’nai Or and the Shalom Center in 1993.

notes.t: An organizational expression of Renewal, not every Renewal participant.

entry.name: Hira
entry.role: Mountain setting near Mecca · Islam · no map point
entry.desc: The setting of the first-revelation tradition. No cave coordinate is supplied.

entry.title: Pakistan’s 1974 classification
entry.text: Pakistan’s constitutional amendment classified Ahmadis as non-Muslims. A state action, not a change in adherents’ self-identification.

entry.name: A global Anglican network
entry.desc: Overseas mission and later provincial autonomy formed a global Anglican network, not one permanent English jurisdiction. Shown as an ordered list, not a drawn route: no surveyed path or geocoded waypoint is supported.

entry.name: Baghdad
entry.desc: The official Bahá’í history places Bahá’u’lláh’s announcement here in 1863. Not the same as ancient Babylon.

entry.name: Reform / Progressive Judaism
entry.blurb: Reform developed in nineteenth-century Germany and spread internationally, adapting inherited practice to new settings.

notes.t: An umbrella, not the name of every national organization. Seesen (1810) and Hamburg (1818) are early milestones, not one founding act for all Reform communities.

entry.name: Ahmadiyya Muslim Community
entry.blurb: The Community identifies itself as Muslim and dates its founding by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad to 1889.

notes.t: The Community’s self-name and self-identification as Muslim. Its Messiah claim is adherents’ belief.

External classification: USCIRF’s 2026 report records Pakistan’s 1974 constitutional classification of Ahmadis as non-Muslims. A dated state classification in one jurisdiction, not a worldwide consensus and not this atlas’s verdict.

entry.title: Hasidism develops
entry.text: Hasidism develops as a Jewish mystical movement around Israel Baal Shem Tov and his disciples. Dynastic succession and biographical legends are not set out here.
entry.whenText: Eighteenth century; no single founding day
entry.side: Eastern Europe · regional context, no map point

entry.name: Sunni Islam
entry.blurb: Sunni interpretation gives authority to the Qur’an, prophetic practice and scholarly consensus.
entry.whenText: Developed after the 632 succession question; no single founding date

notes.t: A classification, not a shared founding-date claim. Not two complete modern denominations appearing in 632.

entry.name: Stone–Campbell movement
entry.blurb: The Stone and Campbell movements sought Christian unity and restoration through their nineteenth-century movement.

notSame.t: Joseph Smith’s restoration movement: shared restoration language does not establish a common institutional parent.

notes.t: The Disciples’ chronology keeps the 31 December handshake and the 1 January union as two dates in one merger history.
